Chris:

I can't vouch for the veracity of these comma-delimited data, but Edgar
Moser from Louisiana State Univ. posted a website in 2001 claiming to
have 4 data sets (Laake's stake data (by individual observer and
pooled), duck nests, half-normal simulated, Hemingway's impala) from the
Introduction to Distance Sampling text and the earlier 1980 Burnham et
al. monograph at this website:

http://www.stat.lsu.edu/faculty/moser/exst7024/transects/TransectData.html

messages.subject: Re: Data sets from Intro to Distance Sampling
parts:
Hi Chris,

Several are available as example projects in Distance (see the last page of
Chapter 3 of the online help) and can easily be exported to other software.

The mrds analysis engine in Distance is actually an R library (see Chapter 10 of
the online help, under "Running the MRDS Analysis Engine from Outside Distance);
it can analyze single platform as well as double platform data (although at
present it only does key functions for detection functions and not adjustment
terms). So, this might make a nice way to check your own R code.

Cheers, - Len
